full_judgment: 3. Mr. Manzil Murshid, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners submitted that none in the past came before the Court challenging the allocation of the symbols `scales' though it was installed allocated by the commission in 1972 but there is no limitation in public interest litigation although the symbol had been allocated since December, 1972. Moreover, it was allocated to a party who are using the symbol though the said party deserved to be banned to participate in politics due to their involvement in the anti-liberation movement. He further submitted that although the symbol is allocated during the election period yet it is used by a political party always in their banners, festoons, leaflet, flyer, letter pad and Court pin and rubber stamp, souvenir and also in their party office building as its own monogram. He also submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in rejecting the application as because the 'impugned Rule 9(1) of conduct of election Rules, 1972 in respect of 'scales' issued by SRO No.223- Ain/2001 published on 20.08.2001 in the gazette without considering that the 'scales' is the symbol of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, a site of justice. Finally, the learned Advocate submitted that the 'scales' is as well used in the official pad of the Supreme Court, in every chair of the Judges, in the calendar of the Supreme Court and in all its publications. Moreover, 'scales' is also used in the flag of the car of the Judges of the Supreme Court, if some other used it, confusion may be created amongst the people which may undermine the status, dignity, prestige and authority of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.
